blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Lazarus was sick, and his sisters, Martha and Mary, sent word to Jesus. By the time Jesus reached their village of Bethany, Lazarus had died.

verses.text: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Bethany was close to Jerusalem, only a short walk away. Many friends had come out from the city to sit with the two sisters. A house in grief is heavy and slow, full of tears and quiet visits.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him on the road. Mary stayed in the house. Martha said what had been sitting on her heart.

verses.text: Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

segments.speaker: martha
segments.text: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Even in her pain, Martha still trusted him. She said she knew God would give him whatever he asked. Jesus told her that her brother would rise again. Martha said yes, she knew he would rise at the last day. Then Jesus turned her eyes from a far-off day to himself.

verses.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

verses.text: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He asked her if she believed this. Martha did not hold back.

verses.text: She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.

segments.speaker: martha
segments.text: Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Then Martha went home and quietly told her sister that the Master had come and was calling for her. Mary got up at once and went out to him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The friends who had been comforting her saw her hurry out, and they followed, thinking she was going to the grave to weep. When Mary came to Jesus, she fell down at his feet and said the very same words her sister had said.

verses.text: Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him,

segments.speaker: mary
segments.text: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus saw her weeping. He saw the friends weeping with her. He did not hurry their sorrow or tell them to stop. He groaned in his spirit and was troubled, and he asked where they had laid him. They said, come and see.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Two words, and the shortest verse in the whole Bible. Jesus knew what he was about to do, and still he wept with them.

verses.text: Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him!

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Some of them wondered why the man who had opened the eyes of the blind could not have kept his friend from dying. Jesus, groaning again, came to the grave. It was a cave, with a stone laid across it.

verses.text: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him,

segments.speaker: martha
segments.text: Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: It was an honest worry. Four days is a long time. Jesus answered her gently, reminding her of what he had told her on the road.

verses.text: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: So they took away the stone. Jesus lifted up his eyes and thanked his Father for hearing him. He prayed out loud, so that the people standing there might believe that the Father had sent him.

verses.text: And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.

verses.text: And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The same Jesus who wept at the grave called a dead man out of it. He did not skip past their grief, and death did not have the last word. The one who weeps with us is the resurrection and the life.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to John 11:17-44; Jesus's words stay in scripture blocks; removed the draft's invented detail (grave clothes falling away) and a near-"speak life" phrase.

cultural.note: Grief shown as heavy and real, not hurried; plain voice.

qa.rewritten: Free draft invented the ending detail; rewritten close to the text.
